items.title: GTA 6 squeaks into eligibility for The Game Awards 2026 by the smallest of margins - but can it break Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's record number of wins?
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 releases 19th November and The Game Awards cut-off is 20th November. It's a close call. But will GTA 6 win?
items.content:
Image credit: Rockstar News by Robert Purchese Associate Editor Published on Oct. 15, 2026, 4:10 p.m. Follow Grand Theft Auto VI Prioritise us on Google This generation's mega-game, Grand Theft Auto 6 , will be eligible for The Game Awards 2026 by a matter of one day.

As highlighted on X by industry watcher Shinobi602 , the cut-off date for this year's The Game Awards is 20th November, meaning GTA 6 - which arrives on 19th November - can be nominated across the show's various categories in 2026 and can potentially win. "Games must be made commercially available to customers on or before Friday, November 20, 2026, at 9pm PT," The Game Awards' website FAQ states.

The fit is so snug it might appear an exception has been made for Rockstar's game, but as Shinobi602 also noted , cut-off dates have been pretty similar each year, varying only by a day or two.

With GTA 6 in contention, the question becomes one of how much it could dominate proceedings. Rewind to Rockstar's last big release - Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018 - and that game took home four awards : Best Narrative, Best Audio Design, Best Score/Music, and Best Performance (won by Roger Clark for his portrayal of protagonist Arthur Morgan).

The current TGA record holder - the game to beat - is Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , which last year took home nine wins , including the coveted Game of the Year award. Before Clair Obscur, the previous leader was Baldur's Gate 3 , with six wins. GTA 6 is an order of magnitude larger in terms of budget, scope, and public anticipation than either game, especially Clair Obscur. The weight of expectation is on Rockstar, that's for sure.

The Game Awards 2026 takes place on 10th December, and usually bookends the year's industry activity, after which we all frantically try to decide what our personal games of the year are. Eurogamer, for full disclosure, is a member of The Game Awards jury, along with many other gaming websites.

Meanwhile, Rockstar released a new launch trailer for GTA 6 this afternoon, highlighting Jason and Lucia's steamy relationship - literally, as they frolic in the shower - and the strain of being in a high-stakes crime environment such as theirs.

Rockstar is also currently embroiled in an employment tribunal in Scotland revolving around the sudden firing of 31 staff from Rockstar North last year. Those affected call it union-busting, whereas Rockstar insists employees were fired for gross misconduct. The verdict is now not expected until well into November , almost bang on when GTA 6 releases.

items.title: You Can Now Play Battlefield 6 and More on Xbox Game Pass
items.summary: However, Clair Obscur is now gone from the service.
items.content:
However, Clair Obscur is now gone from the service.

Microsoft Xbox Game Pass subscribers can jump into huge battles now in Battlefield 6 . That’s good because, Microsoft removed one of CNET’s best games of 2025 , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , from the service. Maybe Battlefield 6 and the other games arriving this month will have what it takes to fill the Clair Obscur-sized hole in my heart.

Xbox Game Pass , a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X , Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 a month . With a subscription to the higher-tiered Game Pass Ultimate ( $23 a month ), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month.

Here are all the games Microsoft is adding to Xbox Game Pass in the first half of October 2026.

Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play now.

CNET’s David Lumb called this installment in the popular Battlefield series a “riveting shooter.” It’s full of huge multiplayer battles, close-quarters combat and loads of gunfights and explosions. While most people will gravitate towards multiplayer, there is a single-player campaign if you want a break from the online mayhem.

In this first-person soulslike game, you’re a soldier in Napoleon’s army who dies. No worries, because you’re back from the dead with a handful of supernatural abilities that you wield in your left hand, like in the almost 20-year-old game BioShock . You’ll use these skills to battle monsters and uncover a conspiracy that could threaten all of humanity.

Bluey’s Happy Snaps proves that not every game coming to Game Pass has to be full of action. You’ll unwind and explore Bluey’s world while taking photos in areas familiar to anyone who’s seen the popular children’s show – let’s be honest, this show’s also popular with adults. You can take photos on your own, or play with a partner, friend or your kid as you turn in-game moments into fun.

Those are a few of the games Microsoft is bringing to Game Pass in October. Here are the rest of the games you’ll see on the service soon.

Microsoft also removed nine games from Xbox Game Pass, including the award-winning Clair Obscur. So you’ll have to buy these games separately now if you still want to play them.

For more on Xbox, check out our Xbox Game Pass review , learn which Game Pass plan is right for you and discover what other games you can play on the service.

items.title: The 10 Most Underrated RPGs of the Last Decade, Ranked
items.content:
By Jason Venter Published Oct 14, 2026, 9:30 PM EDT Polygon Lists Rich rewards lie off the beaten path

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There’s something about the RPG genre. These games tell amazing stories players want to experience time and time again, are populated by memorable characters, and often explore deep themes — even if their heroes do tend to have memory problems, spiky hair, and swords the size of New Jersey.

A truly great RPG is a generational treat. Players flock to the newest Final Fantasy, or to acclaimed newcomers like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Metaphor: ReFantazio . But there have been plenty of other great games released over the last ten years or so, and they didn’t always receive the attention they should have. Here is our list of 10 of the most underrated RPGs of the last decade, ready to point you toward some of the very best experiences you may have missed.

Image: Nihon Falcom/GungHo Online Entertainment Available on: Switch, Switch 2, PS5, PC

The original release of Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter happened way back in 2004 in Japan, where it was known as Eiyuu Densetsu: Sora no Kiseki . In 2011, a localized version finally came to North America, courtesy of Xseed Games. Then followed the PC port in 2014. Recently, Falcom finally returned to its classic series, producing an ambitious remake that blends action and turn-based combat, while retaining the rich world and epic scale that made the previous versions so great. A remake of the second chapter followed earlier this year . While both games launched to rave reviews and have found a passionate audience among players in the know, they’re not being talked about in the same breath as behemoths like Final Fantasy. Don’t sleep on them.

Ever since Harvest Moon launched on the Super Famicom in 1996, the world has had a passion for virtual farming that defies easy explanation. Stardew Valley has kept that passion alive, alongside new and remade Story of Seasons entries, and there have been numerous other cozy sim games along the way. Sometimes, developers mix the classic farming with RPG elements, as in Rune Factory . Then there is Harvestella , an action-RPG from Live Wire that takes that second approach. It provides 12 character classes, including standards like the fighter and the mage, and finds the hero managing a farm while interacting with the locals living in a village called Lethe. There are deep RPG elements, along with an intriguing plot to accompany all the farming, cooking, crafting, and fishing.

Image: Nippon Ichi Software/NIS America Available on: Switch, PS4, Vita, PC

Not everyone likes the old-school style of RPG that takes place from a first-person perspective and primarily confines itself to dungeon crawling. But if you have always appreciated games like Wizardry and Etrian Odyssey , Labyrinth of Refrain: Coven of Dusk is another one to check out. Originally released on PlayStation Vita in Japan in 2016, the game came to North America on Switch, PlayStation 4, and PC a couple of years later. It casts you as a magical book with the ability to create a brigade of puppet soldiers to do your bidding. The story concerns finding a way to revive a deceased loved one, but the moment-to-moment combat and exploration are what will keep players coming back. A sequel, Labyrinth of Galleria: The Moon Society , followed in 2020.

Image: Lancarse/Square Enix Available on: Switch, PS4, PS5, PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X

Having Square Enix as its publisher seems like it should practically guarantee an RPG success, but that’s not what happened for The DioField Chronicle . Despite featuring a rich plot exploring the consequences of war, along with free-flowing combat that mixed real-time strategy with tactics, the game seems largely to have gone unnoticed by players who might have loved it if they gave it a chance. Square Enix didn’t only publish the game, but contributed to its development alongside Lancarse ( Shin Megami Tensei: Strange Journey ). Character art, for instance, was produced by Isamu Kamikokuryo ( Final Fantasy 12 ). Fans looking around for something to keep them busy after they finish Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave need look no further than The DioField Chronicle .

Image: Lancarse/NIS America Available on: Switch, PS4, PS5, PC

Developed by Lancarse, a studio that frequently seems to struggle to find a wide audience for its games, Monark takes place within Shin Mikado Academy. The high school is sealed away from the outside world, shrouded in a maddening mist powered by demonic forces. To free themselves, the students must defeat the monsters by venturing into an Otherworld, which can only mean one thing: lots of combat. Although it received some criticism for the amount of grinding necessary to progress, the game’s systems and abilities are definite high points. The dark scenario, co-written by Fuyuki Hayashi ( Crystar ) and overseen by Kazunari Suzuki (the early Shin Megami Tensei games), recalls genre classics. There’s also a somber soundtrack that delighted players who gave the game a chance. It may not be a visual stunner, but there’s enough going for it to entertain RPG players willing to look past its rough exterior.

Image: Rabbit and Bear Studios Available on: Switch, PS4, PS5, PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X

Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes was announced on Kickstarter back in 2020 as an attempt to produce a spiritual successor to the Suikoden series, since Konami didn’t seem interested in doing much with that property at the time. Developed by the newly formed Rabbit & Bear Studios and headed by Yoshitaka Murayama, who created Suikoden and directed its first two games, the game ultimately wound up delivering much of what it promised. Sadly, Murayama passed away on Feb. 6, 2024, just two months before the game’s release. Upon launching, the game was well received by critics and players alike for its engaging plot and familiar gameplay elements, earning general recommendations as an RPG and additional enthusiasm from the dedicated Suikoden fans it was made to please.

items.title: Steam Deck gets "fully functional" Game Boy mod, creator shows it off with Clair Obscur Expedition 33 gameplay
items.summary: Steam Boy is now fully functional, with footage showing Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 running directly on the Game Boy-style handheld.
items.content:
Last Updated on October 14, 2026 PC Guide is reader-supported. When you buy through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Read More Table of Contents Running Clair Obscur on a Game Boy-style Steam Deck Latest tech deals. A couple of months ago, a Steam Deck modder showed off an ambitious project that involved squeezing the handheld’s hardware into a device roughly the size of a classic Game Boy. At the time, the project was still a work in progress, with one major problem left to solve: getting its custom display to actually work. Now, the creator has returned with some good news, confirming that the Steam Boy is now fully functional.

The project comes from Reddit user PhyFawkes, who originally started experimenting with the idea after realizing how small the Steam Deck’s motherboard actually is. The goal was to build a much smaller handheld while keeping as much of the original Steam Deck hardware as possible. The result is a Game Boy-sized device that uses the motherboard, battery, speakers, and face buttons from an LCD Steam Deck , along with a thumbstick, D-Pad, and trackpad.

The display was always going to be one of the biggest challenges. The Steam Boy uses a custom 1080 x 1200 AMOLED display running at 90Hz, which is actually a higher resolution than the standard Steam Deck screen. During the earlier stages of the project, the display wasn’t functional, meaning the Steam Boy could only output to an external monitor.

That problem has now been solved. In a new update, PhyFawkes confirmed that the Steam Boy is “now fully functional,” while also sharing footage of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 running directly on the handheld. The creator admitted that getting the display working took some time, but said it wasn’t nearly as impossible as some people had suggested. More technical details about how it was achieved are expected to be shared later.

PhyFawkes also confirmed that almost all of the internals remain unmodified parts taken directly from a Steam Deck. The main exceptions are the new display and the custom adapter PCB required to connect it to the Deck’s motherboard.

Cooling such powerful hardware inside a much smaller body was another challenge. The Steam Boy uses a small 30 x 7mm fan, a heatsink, and a custom 3D-printed mount. Earlier testing showed temperatures in the 70°C range while playing TUNIC, while the system reached around 90°C in Clair Obscur.

Would you buy a cheaper version of the Steam Frame that doesn’t work standalone?

Yes, as long as the price is significantly lower ($750 or less)

Abdul is a tech writer and Editor for PC Guide, specializing in all things tech, gaming, and hardware.

items.title: 8 Games Leave Xbox Game Pass on October 15, Including Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, A Plague Tale: Requiem and six more games leave Xbox Game Pass on October 15. Full list, plus the member discount to keep them.
items.content:
Eight games leave Xbox Game Pass tomorrow, Thursday, October 15, and the biggest name on the list is Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. If you are partway through any of them, today is the day to finish up or buy a copy.

Clair Obscur joined Game Pass on day one in April 2025 and went on to win Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2025, so its exit is the one most subscribers will notice. A Plague Tale: Requiem, Pacific Drive and Evil West are going too.

The Superball perk for members also ends on October 15, but that is a Game Pass perk rather than a game in the library.

Every game on the list currently carries a Game Pass member discount of at least 20% in the Xbox Store. Buying a game you already have installed through Game Pass just unlocks your copy permanently, so there is nothing to download again.

Saves and achievements are tied to your account, not to the subscription. If you buy one of these games later, even after it has left Game Pass, you pick up where you left off.

The big October addition is Battlefield 6, which joined Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass on October 13. Bluey’s Happy Snaps and Chained Beasts arrive on October 15, the same day these eight games leave, and Beyond These Stars follows on October 16.

items.title: Charlie Cox recorded 40 hours for an unnamed Sega game - Voice Over Talent Industry News
items.summary: The Expedition 33 star told IGN he recorded about 40 hours of lines for an unannounced Sega game, in an accent the crew expected from an American.
items.content:
Share Charlie Cox, the Daredevil actor who voiced Gustave in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, told IGN at New York Comic Con that he has already recorded a Sega game with no name. By his count it took about 40 hours of lines, and the crew had been expecting an American.

On October 9, IGN asked Cox whether more video games are coming. He gave no title, no genre and no release window. What he gave instead is a small, honest account of what a big game session is like for the actor in the chair.

“I did another one! It doesn’t have a name yet. I did a Sega one. I’ve done one since. It hasn’t come out yet. It was fun to do. It’s hard. It’s a whole different job, man,” Cox told IGN, according to Gaming Bolt’s transcript of the interview.

On screen Cox is Matt Murdock, the Daredevil of Marvel’s streaming shows. In games he is Gustave, the lead of Sandfall Interactive’s Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the role that earned him a Best Performance nomination at the 2025 Game Awards.

He said he wasn’t sure how much he was allowed to say, and then said a good deal anyway. By his account he agreed to the Sega job before he had met the people making it, then turned up for the first day of a recording commitment that ran to roughly 40 hours.

Image: Sandfall Interactive, Kepler Interactive

The detail that has spread is the accent. Cox is English, and he says nobody at the studio had worked that out. He tells it as a scene: he walks in and greets the room in his own voice. “Hi guys, nice to meet you! How are you?” And then, he says, “all of them went, ‘…oh, he’s English.’”

The team had “wanted him to be American,” he explained. So the first day was not only the first day of recording. It was the day he had to turn the part into an American one on the spot. “Yeah, I think they thought I was American,” he said.

The scale is the story. Kotaku quotes him saying he “had to do 40 hours or whatever it was,” and it is worth remembering that this is an actor recalling a long stretch of work, not reading from a contract.

Set that beside his last game. In June 2025, speaking at Washington State Summer Con, he said of Expedition 33: “My agent asked me if I wanted to go and do some voiceover [and] I was in the studio for four hours maybe,” in a clip Push Square reported . He added that he hadn’t played the game. By his own rough numbers, the Sega job is ten times as much recording.

He hinted at the jump months ago. In March, according to Spanish outlet LevelUp, Cox said in an interview that he would take part in another game this year in which he would be far more involved, with a lot more work.

Charlie Cox, on recording a video game, to IGN at New York Comic Con Why an unprepared accent is a hard day Reading a script cold is an ordinary day in a booth. Reading it cold in an accent that isn’t yours is not. Cox says the lines were ones he had “not prepared in an accent,” and the problem is not only getting them right once. A lead character appears across dozens of hours of play, and game lines are often recorded out of story order, so the accent has to sit in the same place on every take, whether it is the first line of the day or the last.

Image: Sandfall Interactive, Behind the Voices (an Expedition 33 session, not the Sega game)

That is Voice Over Herald’s reading of the craft, not Cox’s own explanation. What he says himself is shorter: it is hard, and it is a different job from the one he does for a camera.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 makes an appearance in Astral Ascent
items.summary: Astral Ascent, the roguelite platformer featuring lightning-fast combat and co-op play, has just received a very prestigious collaboration. The world…
items.content:
Astral Ascent , the roguelite platformer featuring lightning-fast combat and co-op play, has just received a very prestigious collaboration. The world of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has made an appearance in the game from Hibernian Workshop.

This free update adds six new summons, three bosses, two music tracks, and three rooms drawn from the world of Sandfall Interactive’s game. Esquie also makes an appearance.

A trailer has been released. Astral Ascent is available on PS5, PS4, Switch, and PC.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Comes To Astral Ascent In New Crossover Update
items.content:
We've been patiently hoping that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 would make its way to Switch 2 ever since it consumed our every waking hour last year. Sandfall is still yet to make that happen, but in the meantime, we have a crossover with the wonderful roguelike Astral Ascent , which we can play right now.

As revealed in today's Triple-i Initiative showcase, the sublime platforming roguelike has been treated to a bunch of crossover content from the land of Lumière. This includes three brand new bosses (Golgra, the Mime and Pétank), new rooms inspired by the game, and recruitable Expedition ally summons, each of which comes with its own special skills.

Truthfully, it looks wonderful. The crossover brings Expedition 33's world into Astral Ascent's glorious pixel art, and the trailer alone was enough to bring a tear to this writer's eye.

Here's the full rundown of everything included in the update, as detailed on the Astral Ascent Steam page:

Three Exclusive Bosses Golgra, the Mime, and Pétank have invaded the Prison, each with brand-new combat mechanics built just for this crossover. - Golgra - Calm at first, but her kicks and gestral allies get brutal once her second phase kicks in. - The Mime - Hammers, nails, walls take them both down together, or they'll revive each other. - Pétank - Runs, then rains projectiles, clones, and explosions on you.

Three New Rooms Straight from the world of Expedition 33 : Lumière , the Gestral Village , and the Campfire . One appears at random before the final boss each run: pick Expedition 33 content or the Andromeda Bar, but choose fast, it won't come back this run!

Around the Campfire Recruit a member of the Expedition as a special summon, each with their own unique mechanic: - Gustave - Heals, boosts your attack, strikes with you, and charges up a devastating finisher. - Maelle - Shifts stance with your HP; hold one long enough for a powerful payoff attack. - Sciel - Draws cards : Moon for mana, Sun for direct strikes, Twilight for a big hit. - Lune - Casts elemental spells matching your build, building to a powerful finisher. - Verso - Rank rises on hit, drops on damage taken, push it high for a massive attack bonus. - Monoco - Draws a random card, each triggering a different monster summon. You'll only get one Expedition ally per run, so take your pick, and don't forget to give Esquie a hug!

All of this is available for free to everyone who has beaten Astral Ascent on Destiny Level 0. What an excuse to dive back in, eh?

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 "broke" T-Pain with its "too sad" intro: "It gets worse? Absolutely not"
items.summary: Might I recommend The Last of Us?
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Sandfall Interactive) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Some people just aren't built to endure the kind of bleak, unrelenting tragedy that often exists at the bottom of a great story's emotional arc. Rapper T-Pain may just have that affliction, having recently started Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on his Nappy Boy Gaming YouTube channel and noped out after its notoriously sad opening sequence.

*Spoilers for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 below. Turn back if you haven't played through the prologue yet.*

In the video just below, you can see T-Pain playing about 15 minutes of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 from the very start, which of course means he witnesses the awfully tragic death of Sophie in the prologue, leaving him speechless for a few seconds as he resumes control of Gustave. T-Pain eventually makes an exacerbated "shewwww" sound and exits to desktop. "Is it a sad story?" an offscreen person says, clearly noticing T-Pain's emotional exhaustion. "Yeah."

"Yeah, it was too sad," T-Pain responds, laughing. Just before ending the video, the rapper appears to read a comment on his stream warning him that, "it gets worse" – and anyone who's played through the game knows it absolutely does get worse, and soon – and T-Pain decides then and there, "Absolutely not."

I never want to play the best-written Blood of Dawnwalker mission ever again The 25 best video game stories of all time Troy Baker says The Last of Us 2's devastating final scene was originally at the start of the game This Game Broke T-Pain - YouTube Watch On I totally get his reluctance to continue here. Sometimes I just want to play a game, or watch a movie, or read a book, and not feel like I need to text my therapist. Unfortunately, in my view, if a story's writing and performances are effective enough to evoke such powerful emotion, it's probably worth seeing through, even if it never provides the sort of emotional upswing you want.

The Last of Us is one of my all-time favorite stories across all mediums precisely because it offers such an uncompromising, realistic account of two normal people trying to navigate a zombie apocalypse. Bad things are going to happen to good people, and there won't always be a picture-perfect redemption for anyone. Casting aside the conventional trajectories of heroes and villains makes for a much more believable, and thus absorbing story. You might not be moving your body like a cyclone afterwards, but you can always get low with something a little lighter to balance things out.

items.title: 'It's Incredibly Well-Made, But…' — Former PlayStation Boss Warned Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Devs It Would Be 'Overlooked' if They Called It a Turn-Based RPG
items.summary: Former PlayStation lead Shuhei Yoshida warned the developers behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 about calling it a "turn-based RPG" because "that alone might cause players to overlook it.
items.content:
Former PlayStation lead Shuhei Yoshida warned the developers behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 about calling it a "turn-based RPG" because "that alone might cause players to overlook it."

Yoshida, who served as PlayStation's head of indies and president of Sony Interactive Entertainment Worldwide Studios before stepping down in 2024, spoke about some key advice he gave the award-winning team during a recent lecture for indie game developers. Portions of that lecture were then reported by 4Gamer and subsequently translated by Automaton , including one piece of advice he gave to publisher Kepler Interactive while advising the team ahead of its April 2025 launch.

"It’s incredibly well-made, but it would be better not to call it a turn-based RPG," Yoshida warned the Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs. "That alone might cause players to overlook it."

But why? Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 went on to receive praise from fans and critics (including a 9/10 review from IGN), while ending its already explosive year with big wins across The Game Awards , BAFTA , DICE , and IGN award shows. Its positive reception was so intense that even the developers at Sandfall Interactive weren't prepared for its towering Metacritic score .

Yoshida acknowledged Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 as a quality release long before it reached the hands of the public. He was impressed early on, calling attention to its "combination of turn-based JRPG mechanics and real-time action inputs reminiscent of The Legend of Dragoon." The problem, however, was that, at the time, he was concerned its success could be affected by what he observed to be a tendency for turn-based JRPGs to be seen as outdated.

Game-award-winning formula or not, Yoshida feared Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 would be ignored by some gamers if they saw that "turn-based" label. As a result, Kepler got creative and instead started selling Sandfall's first game as an experience with "reactive turn-based battles" instead, and the rest is history.

The game, of course, went on to become a massive sales success despite its proximity to the launch of The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion . Yoshida said he's since noticed an uptick in reports from publishers receiving pitches for new turn-based RPGs.

While we wait to see what's next from Yoshida and Sandfall, you can see why the developers behind Final Fantasy Resonance think turn-based RPGs are making a huge comeback . You can also read the devs' conversation about canon endings and the writer who got their start at Sandfall .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: Patch v1.5.6 is now live!
items.summary: Expeditioners, Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic! Content New supported language (text): Arabic [/*] Credi
items.content:
Expeditioners,

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!

Content

  • New supported language (text): Arabic

    [/*]

  • Credits updated (new linguists, testers and fonts)

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Fixed an issue where applying burn after an enemy has been stunned causes them to be able to act immediately after recovering from the stun.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Cleim weapon level 10 Lumina effect that does not trigger correctly on every instance of area of effect skills.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Martenon’s Lumina effects that do not work if Sciel does not have two consecutive turns.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Sireso weapon, Level 4 Lumina, and Powerful buff, from Pictos/Luminas, applied at the start of battle may override each other depending on the character's position in combat.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Chromatic Lampmaster's AOE skill missing a sound cue on the jump attack.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Sirene's Widow Ballet missing SFX during second charm attack.

    [/*]

  • Fixed characters in combat that may have displaced heads in Photo Mode if they were not seen while turning on Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Various minor fixes of the UI and localizations.

    [/*]

We are aware of a crash affecting some of you when loading into the Reacher or going out of the Manor. This crash is related to some specific PC configurations. Until we fix this issue, you can work around it by setting ‘Global Illumination’ to anything below ‘Epic’ temporarily.

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Dispatch are now available together in a 10% off bundle! 

Bundle art by Derek Stratton

This is a really special bundle for us - since its release, Dispatch left such an impact on us and immediately became one of our favourites.   

Our games are quite different, but we couldn’t help ourselves - and ultimately, we just want more people to discover the powerful stories and artistry behind these games.

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: Patch v1.5.3 is live!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below: Update On Sirene Crash After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer b
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below:

Update On Sirene Crash

  • After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer be reproduced on our end. If you keep getting this issue, we’d suggest updating your Windows to the latest version. If the issue persists, please submit a report and we’ll continue investigating.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes & Improvements

Photo Mode

  • Fixed facial hair of characters being blurred in the Photo Mode on the close distance if Shading was set to Epic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue in Photo mode that prevented the Inner Cone Angle and Outer Cone Angle options from affecting the shape of the preview light source.

    [/*]

  • Photo Mode's spotlight and point light display has been modified to improve their visibility

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where loading a save while picking up a journal could cause that journal to disappear permanently and become impossible to collect again.

    • Missing journals are now also restored retroactively when loading affected saves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft lock that could occur, during the Chromatic Glissando encounter in Sirene’s Dress level, when a dead expeditioner equipped with Shortcut and Second Chance pictos was swallowed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on Gestral Beach where using the Rematch option after losing the volleyball minigame could create a blocked save.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a visual issue where characters affected by Inverted would not have the correct colour effect applied to their eyes.

    [/*]

Environment

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various lighting issues on Steam Deck in Verso’s Drafts, Endless Tower and Stone Wave Cliffs levels.

    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team
